articles.title: Homem é encontrado boiando e em parada cardiorrespiratória em enchente | G1
articles.standfirst: Vítima, de 60 anos, foi resgatada por bombeiros com o uso de uma balsa inflável e levada ao Pronto-Socorro Central de São Vicente.
articles.summary: Enchente em São Vicente mobiliza bombeiros para resgatar homem de 50 anos encontrado em parada cardiorrespiratória e levado ao Pronto-Socorro.
articles.body:
Sá Catarina de Moraes, em São Vicente (imagem ilustrativa) — Foto: Arquivo/Leandro Ferreira/VC no G1

Um homem, de 60 anos, morreu após ser encontrado boiando em um córrego durante uma enchente no Parque São Vicente , em São Vicente, no litoral de São Paulo, na madrugada deste sábado (12).

Ele foi resgatado e levado ao Pronto-Socorro Central pelo Corpo de Bombeiros. De acordo com a Secretaria de Segurança Pública (SSP), a vítima teve a morte atestada no hospital.

A ocorrência foi registrada neste sábado (12), por volta das 2h28, na Rua Lourival Moreira do Amaral. Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, o homem estava inconsciente e em parada cardiorrespiratória quando foi resgatado.

Após ser retirado da água, ele ficou aos cuidados de uma equipe avançada do Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) e foi encaminhado ao PS Central de São Vicente.

De acordo com o Corpo de Bombeiros, a corporação foi acionada para apoiar o Samu no atendimento à vítima, que havia sido localizada em meio à enchente que atingiu o córrego.

Segundo os bombeiros, três agentes participaram da ocorrência. Por causa das condições do local, a equipe utilizou uma balsa inflável para chegar até o homem e retirá-lo da água. As causas e as circunstâncias da ocorrência ainda são desconhecidas e deverão ser apuradas pelas autoridades.

A perícia foi acionada e o caso foi registrado como morte suspeita na Delegacia de São Vicente.

articles.title: Grávida de 7 meses morre após carro capotar na BR-402, em Morros (MA) | G1
articles.standfirst: Luana Sudário Mota Amaral, de 37 anos, estava com o marido e duas crianças e seguia para Humberto de Campos. Segundo informações preliminares, veículo saiu da pista durante tentativa de desviar de buraco.
articles.summary: Luana Sudário Mota Amaral, de 37 anos, estava com o marido e duas crianças e seguia para Humberto de Campos.
articles.body:
Grávida de 7 meses morre após carro capotar na BR-402, em Morros — Foto: Divulgação/Redes sociais

Uma mulher de 37 anos, grávida de sete meses, morreu após um acidente na BR-402, nas proximidades do povoado Arrudinha, no município de Morros , na região do Munim, no Maranhão. O acidente aconteceu no fim da manhã dessa sexta-feira (11).

A vítima foi identificada como Luana Sudário Mota Amaral. Segundo informações preliminares, ela dirigia um Fiat Siena vermelho quando o veículo saiu da pista e capotou.

Luana morava em São Luís e seguia para Humberto de Campos para um passeio em família. No carro também estavam o marido dela e duas crianças.

Carro teria capotado durante desvio de buraco

De acordo com as informações apuradas até o momento, Luana trafegava pela BR-402 quando tentou desviar de um buraco na rodovia, nas proximidades do povoado Arrudinha.

Durante a manobra, ela teria perdido o controle da direção. O veículo saiu da pista e capotou. Com a força do acidente, Luana foi arremessada para fora do automóvel.

As circunstâncias exatas que provocaram o acidente ainda deverão ser esclarecidas.

Após o acidente, Luana foi socorrida e encaminhada para uma Unidade de Pronto Atendimento (UPA) em Morros. Por causa da gravidade dos ferimentos, Luana não resistiu e morreu. Ela estava no sétimo mês de gestação. O bebê também não sobreviveu.

Luana trabalhava na área da saúde como enfermeira em São Luís.

articles.title: Mulher que criou sebo 'viajante’ inaugura unidade fixa em Itapetininga | G1
articles.standfirst: Novo espaço fica localizado na Rua Bernardino de Campos, na região central de Itapetininga. Evento de inauguração é neste sábado (12), das 11h às 18h, com entrada gratuita.
articles.summary: O novo espaço fica localizado na Rua Bernardino de Campos, na região central de Itapetininga. O evento de inauguração será neste sábado (12), das 11h às 18h, com entrada gratuita.
articles.body:
Mais do que contar histórias, os livros podem aproximar pessoas, despertar novos interesses e criar comunidades entre leitores. Ao redor das páginas, também surgem amizades, trocas de experiências e iniciativas que ajudam a fortalecer a cultura e o acesso à leitura.

Foi a partir dessa paixão pelos livros que Maria Gabriela Moura, de 37 anos, moradora de Itapetininga (SP), começou sua jornada no empreendedorismo. Ela criou um “sebo viajante”, usando uma mala para transportar os livros e levá-los a diferentes lugares , com a proposta de tornar a leitura mais acessível.

Dois anos depois de inaugurar uma “banca de livros”, Maria começa um novo capítulo de sua história neste sábado (12): o sebo ganhou um espaço próprio e mais amplo na cidade. O evento será das 11h às 18h, com entrada gratuita.

Antes, Maria reunia e compartilhava diferentes títulos com moradores e visitantes na Praça do Rosário. Agora, o “Viaje com os Livros” está em um novo endereço, na Rua Bernardino de Campos, 62, no Centro de Itapetininga.

“Está sendo incrível. É como uma página em branco. Nós pensávamos nessa possibilidade, mas as coisas aconteceram naturalmente”, contou Maria Gabriela ao g1 .

Moradora de Itapetininga (SP) inaugura novo espaço de leitura neste sábado (12) — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

O anúncio do novo espaço foi publicado nas redes sociais do sebo na quinta-feira (10).

“Nossos leitores são tantos, nossas histórias cresceram tanto e o Viaje foi tão longe que agora temos uma casa. A banca fecha, mas o Viaje abre as portas de uma nova casa e novas oportunidades”, compartilhou.

A antiga banca, que durante dois anos ocupou a Praça do Rosário, agora dá lugar a um espaço maior e fixo no Centro de Itapetininga.

“A banca fechou, agora ela vai abençoar outro empreendedor. Eu vejo como um reconhecimento de toda a minha luta pela leitura, de muito trabalho e dedicação. Está sendo incrível ver esse movimento literário em Itapetininga”, compartilhou Maria.

Quem quiser conhecer o novo espaço já pode aproveitar a inauguração neste sábado, durante o tradicional “Deu a Loka no Sebo”. A atração reúne livros com preços a partir de R$ 1.

Além dos livros, o evento terá venda de doces e salgados e espaço para aquele cafezinho. A inauguração começa às 11h e segue até as 18h.

“Por ora, estamos nos reorganizando. Espero que todos encontrem um refúgio para desacelerar, degustar um livro com calma e bater aquele papo gostoso”, disse a proprietária.

A relação de Maria Gabriela com os livros começou em 2016, quando ela criou o sebo, que reúne exemplares doados ou vendidos a preços acessíveis. A paixão pela leitura também deu origem a um projeto em que ela “esquecia” livros pela cidade, como forma de incentivar o hábito de ler.

O sebo foi criado em 2016 após um evento em Itapetininga, onde Maria levou os livros dentro de uma mala. A "banca" de livros na região central foi inaugurada em 2024, após a moradora sentir falta de sebos no município.

Maria Gabriela Moura, de 35 anos, cria 'sebo viajante' em Itapetininga (SP) — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal/Maria Gabriela

Inicialmente, o projeto funcionava apenas com a doação de livros. Depois, Maria passou a adotar o modelo de “pague quanto puder”, como forma de ajudar a cobrir os custos dos eventos dos quais participava.

Em cerca de um ano, a iniciativa cresceu e ela começou a ser procurada por pessoas interessadas em comprar os livros. Foi então que Maria decidiu transformar o projeto em um sebo.

Em 2024 ela inaugurou uma banca usada como sebo no Centro de Itapetininga (SP) — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal/Maria Gabriela

A mala com os livros já passou por diversas cidades das regiões de Itapetininga e Sorocaba. Maria Gabriela também participa de festivais de música, feiras e visita escolas para contar como funciona o sebo e levar doações para crianças.

"O objetivo é tornar o livro acessível a todos, livros baratos e de qualidade. Eu procuro ajudar bibliotecas comunitárias, escolas e projetos de incentivo à leitura. Na banca tem livros à venda por apenas R$ 2", conta.

Nas redes sociais, a "livreira" compartilha com os seguidores as edições que estão disponíveis para compra atualmente, assim como os eventos que irá participar.

"Eu faço uma triagem com os livros. Higienizo e separo os gêneros literários. Os valores variam conforme o estado de conservação e a raridade do livro", explica.

Maria Gabriela usa uma mala para transportar livros e cria sebo 'Viaje com os livros' — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal/Maria Gabriela

Há cinco anos, Gabriela tentou alugar uma banca para expandir o sebo, mas não conseguiu. No entanto, em 2024, ela conseguiu realizar o sonho. A banca fica na Praça do Rosário, no Centro de Itapetininga.

Para ela, a banca tem sido a experiência de viver um sonho, pois é possível ter uma interação maior com as pessoas que vão até o local.

"São muitas pessoas que passam para conversar ali, elas me contam sobre o que já leram, batem um papo comigo mesmo", relata.

Em abril do ano passado, Maria Gabriela compartilhou ao g1 o desenvolvimento do projeto onde “esquecia” livros por diversos endereços de Itapetininga. A ação começou em 2016 por Gabriela e, desde então, ela distribuiu mais de três mil edições.

“Esse projeto dá certo até hoje, pois muitas pessoas me ajudaram e ainda ajudam, com doações de livros, na divulgação, comprando e também ‘esquecendo’ livros por aí”, afirma.

Livros são "esquecidos" em diferentes pontos da cidade de Itapetininga (SP) como incentivo a leitura — Foto: Arquivo pessoal/Maria Gabriela Moura

Maria Gabriela conta que escolhe diferentes endereços a fim de conseguir atingir mais públicos: "Peço para amigos também ajudaram a ‘esquecer’, aproveitamos a ida aos lugares que precisamos e deixamos por lá."

Em período de chuva ou com maior umidade do ar, a moradora escolhe lugares cobertos para colocar os livros, assim evitar que o produto estrague e o novo dono aproveite a leitura da melhor maneira.

“A minha única meta é fazer com que o interesse pelo livro não seja esquecido e apagado pelas telas”, concluiu.

Iniciativa criada em 2016, pela Maria Gabriela Moura, já distribuiu mais de três mil livros em Itapetininga (SP) e em outras cidades — Foto: Arquivo pessoal/Maria Gabriela Moura

articles.title: Por que os anos 1980 foram tão coloridos e extravagantes?  | G1
articles.standfirst: Artistas respondiam às crises que atravessavam o mundo, da ditadura militar no Brasil aos anos de Margaret Thatcher no Reino Unido, desafiando padrões de comportamento por meio da moda, dos cabelos, da maquiagem, dos videoclipes e de outras manifestações culturais.
articles.summary: Artistas respondiam às crises que atravessavam o mundo, da ditadura militar no Brasil aos anos de Margaret Thatcher no Reino Unido, desafiando padrões de comportamento por meio da moda, dos cabelos, da maquiagem, dos videoclipes e de outras manifestações culturais.
articles.body:
Michael Jackson canta no Madison Square Garden, em Nova York, durante sua turnê Bad, em 1988 — Foto: Kevin Mazur/Wireimage

Não é só o ChatGPT ou o Gemini que imaginam cores vibrantes, cabelos volumosos e roupas hoje vistas como extravagantes quando pedimos que recriem uma foto como se ela tivesse sido tirada nos anos 1980, parte da trend que viralizou nas redes sociais nesta semana.

Guardados os exageros que a inteligência artificial pode cometer ao tentar imaginar o período, a imagem que temos dos anos 1980 foi real. Ela surgiu, segundo especialistas ouvidos pela BBC News Brasil, do contraste entre as crises que castigavam o mundo na época e a maneira como as pessoas reagiam às dificuldades.

"Esse movimento veio de um cansaço, porque os anos 1970 foram ditatoriais em vários lugares do mundo. Foram difíceis, asfixiantes. Então, nos anos 1980, houve uma espécie de liberação", diz o professor Francisco Homem de Melo, um dos maiores pesquisadores do Brasil na área de design.

No mundo de carne e osso, ainda havia a Guerra Fria entre os Estados Unidos e a União Soviética (URSS); o apartheid que separava brancos e negros na África do Sul; as ditaduras militares que perseguiam milhares na América Latina, inclusive no Brasil; e a crise do HIV e da Aids, que matava no mundo todo.

Por outro lado, no mundo artificial da televisão, Xuxa vestia botas altas, minissaias, ombreiras e roupas cheias de brilho para sair de uma nave cor-de-rosa e comandar um programa na Globo, enquanto o palhaço Bozo armava um verdadeiro circo, com arquibancadas, palcos circulares, grandes letreiros e telefones gigantes, no SBT.

E a extravagância não se limitava aos programas infantis — e tampouco se expressava apenas nos cenários coloridos. Gugu Liberato escolhia o "Rambo brasileiro", realizava os sonhos de fãs com seus ídolos e terminava o programa com uma multidão dançando como passarinhos, enquanto Chacrinha comandava seu Cassino jogando até bacalhau e abacaxi para a plateia.

Na música, os Menudos — que eram porto-riquenhos, mas aprenderam a cantar em português — arrastavam multidões de adolescentes de cabelos volumosos e roupas coloridas, pedindo que ninguém se reprimisse, enquanto Ney Matogrosso radicalizava a transgressão que já era característica à sua carreira ao subir ao palco de rosto pintado e quase sem roupa, só com tapa-sexo, penas, colares e glitter.

Havia ainda Madonna, com seus figurinos e performances cada vez mais provocativos, em trabalhos como Like a Virgin e Like a Prayer ; Michael Jackson, com clipes marcantes como Thriller ; e uma infinidade de outros exemplos que poderiam preencher dezenas de parágrafos e se espalhar pelo mundo.

Madonna se apresenta durante a turnê The Virgin Tour, em Minnesota, nos Estados Unidos, em maio de 1985, usando um vestido brilhante com referências religiosas — Foto: Getty Images/via BBC

Tudo isso enquanto o Brasil, por exemplo, vivia sob a ditadura . Mesmo que já estivesse em processo de abertura, o regime ainda censurava músicas, filmes, peças e programas de televisão, além de perseguir opositores e controlar manifestações políticas.

Mas em vez de representar diretamente as crises políticas e sociais vigentes, boa parte da arte funcionou como uma reação à sobriedade e à funcionalidade que haviam dominado o design e a cultura nas décadas anteriores.

No design, a ideia de que tudo precisava ter uma utilidade, por exemplo, começou a ser questionado pelo movimento pós-modernista. Um dos melhores exemplos disso foi o grupo Memphis, criado na Itália para virar de cabeça para baixo a ideia de que um objeto bonito precisava ser discreto e simples.

Seus integrantes criavam móveis e objetos com cores vibrantes, formas tortas, estampas chamativas e materiais que se pareciam até com brinquedos. Não tinha medo de ser kitsch — como ficou conhecida aquela estética que mistura elementos considerados exagerados, artificiais ou "de mau gosto".

No Reino Unido, outro centro dessa renovação, houve uma explosão musical em meio à dureza dos anos da primeira-ministra Margaret Thatcher, quando os britânicos enfrentavam desemprego, fechamento de fábricas e uma crise que atingia especialmente os trabalhadores.

David Bowie, uma estrela já consolidada desde a década anterior, foi uma das referências visuais para a nova geração do pop britânico.

Um dos principais museus de Londres, o Victoria and Albert Museum (V&A), que abriu no ano passado uma área dedicada ao artista, destaca sua influência e sua maneira de brincar com códigos de gênero por meio de roupas, maquiagem e diferentes personas .

Embora essa influência tenha sido, em alguns casos, mais visual do que musical, artistas e grupos como Duran Duran, Culture Club, Spandau Ballet e Eurythmics vieram na mesma linhagem de um pop que fazia da imagem parte essencial de sua identidade.

O duo britânico Eurythmics, formado por Annie Lennox e Dave Stewart nos anos 1980, em apresentação em Chicaco, nos Estados Unidos, em novembro de 1984 — Foto: Paul Natkin/WireImage

No Brasil, essa mudança de comportamento se expressou principalmente pela música, e sobretudo no Rio de Janeiro, segundo o professor Francisco Homem de Melo, que lecionou na Faculdade de Arquitetura e Urbanismo e de Design da Universidade de São Paulo. A música foi, inclusive, o que influenciou os programas de TV.

O professor explica que, em contraponto aos tropicalistas — a turma de Caetano Veloso, Gilberto Gil e Tom Zé —, que se estabeleceram no fim dos anos 1960 e ao longo dos anos 1970, bandas de pop rock cariocas como Barão Vermelho, Blitz, Kid Abelha e Paralamas do Sucesso passaram a responder à repressão não por meio de protestos, do exílio ou de qualquer militância explícita, mas pelo rompimento com os comportamentos e costumes valorizados pelo regime.

"Essa geração de 80 tinha um cansaço da política partidária e da luta contra a ditadura, a ponto inclusive de ter parecido uma juventude alienada. Não acho que era uma juventude alienada, de jeito nenhum. Eles estavam no Rio, na praia, e queriam chutar o pau da barraca. Queriam curtir um pouco o prazer", diz Chico, como o professor é conhecido e assina seus livros.

"É político também, por vezes até mais estruturalmente político do que uma militância ortodoxa."

Paula Toller, que foi vocalista do Kid Abelha, veste top preto cheio de brilho em show nos anos 1980 — Foto: Getty Images/via BBC

Um dos episódios mais marcantes da trajetória do Barão Vermelho, o show da primeira edição do Rock in Rio, em 1985, ilustra a verve libertária vigente.

A apresentação terminou com Pro Dia Nascer Feliz , com Cazuza dizendo: "Que o dia nasça lindo para todo mundo amanhã. Um Brasil novo, com uma rapaziada esperta". Naquele mesmo dia, o Congresso havia elegido, ainda de forma indireta, Tancredo Neves como o primeiro presidente civil após mais de 20 anos de regime militar.

A visão do professor, também autor do livro Linha do Tempo do Design Gráfico no Brasil , é compartilhada pelo jornalista e apresentador Zeca Camargo, que esteve à frente do lançamento da MTV no país e, depois, apresentou o Fantástico, dominical da Globo que tinha como tradição produzir e lançar videoclipes.

Zeca atribui a estética extravagante à facilidade — e, ao mesmo tempo, às limitações — com que se podia fazer vídeo na época. O videocassete doméstico chegou ao Brasil nessa época, e o VHS rapidamente deixou de ser uma novidade tecnológica para criar um novo mercado de produção e consumo de imagens.

"Mesmo que não se compare com a facilidade de hoje, a maneira como as pessoas podiam gravar e editar estava mais democratizada nos anos 80. Todo mundo tinha uma gravadora de VHS, e na edição trabalhava o quê? Cor, faixas coloridas, bolas, figuras geométricas, porque não tinha a multiplicidade de efeitos de hoje", ele conta.

"Quando todo mundo pode fazer, cada um escolhe sua estética, e a liberdade é colorida."

Essa ruptura também passou pela moda, que retroalimentava a música, o cinema e outras plataformas da cultura pop, em uma década marcada pela valorização de silhuetas mais estruturadas e cores fortes.

A aproximação entre estilistas e estrelas da música ajudou a transformar essas criações em símbolos da década. Jean Paul Gaultier, por exemplo, criou para Madonna o célebre sutiã cônico usado na turnê Blond Ambition , em 1990 — uma peça de corset com duas estruturas pontudas sobre os seios.

Madonna em show em Tóquio em 1990 vestindo figurino criado por Jean-Paul Gaultier — Foto: SYGMA via Getty Images

"São criadores que vestiam sobretudo as mulheres com formas muito geométricas. As mulheres usavam blazers que pareciam armaduras", lembra Zeca, mencionando estilistas como Thierry Mugler, responsável por alguns dos figurinos mais marcantes de artistas como Diana Ross, e Giorgio Armani, que vestiu Richard Gere no filme Gigolô Americano , um clássico da época.

O contraste é grande com a estética que ganhou força nos últimos anos, o chamado quiet luxur y, ou "luxo silencioso", formado por tons neutros, cortes discretos, poucos ou nenhum logotipo e sinais mais sutis de riqueza, presentes nas passarelas, nos figurinos de séries e novelas e nos looks de influenciadores nas redes sociais.

Estética colorida também tinha objetivo mercadológico

O exagero não estava ligado apenas a uma maneira de desafiar o conservadorismo e a sobriedade. Um dos principais teóricos a tentar explicar essa mudança, o filósofo e crítico americano Fredric Jameson, também enxergava nela uma dimensão econômica.

Para Jameson, o chamado pós-modernismo estava ligado às transformações do capitalismo e ao crescimento de uma cultura cada vez mais dominada por imagens, publicidade, mídia e consumo. Em seu ensaio Pós-modernismo: A Lógica Cultural do Capitalismo Tardio , de 1984, ele descreveu o surgimento de uma "nova cultura da imagem".

A estética, nesse cenário, deixava de ser apenas uma característica dos produtos e passava a fazer parte da própria lógica de produção e consumo. A aparência ganhava valor comercial, já que cores, formas, embalagens e imagens ajudavam a diferenciar produtos em um mercado cada vez mais saturado. Quanto maior a quantidade de imagens em circulação, maior a importância de se destacar no meio delas, afinal.

Jameson via esse processo com desconfiança. Uma das características que ele atribuía ao pós-modernismo era o que chamou de "new depthlessness", algo como "nova falta de profundidade", uma cultura em que a superfície, a aparência e a imagem ganhavam um peso cada vez maior.

Para o professor Francisco Homem de Melo, porém, separar arte e mercado é uma tarefa difícil. Ele diz que a chamada poesia marginal, que ganhou força no Rio de Janeiro nos anos 1970, é exemplo disso: embora fosse produzida em pequenas tiragens e circulasse fora dos grandes circuitos editoriais, já envolvia produção, reprodução e venda.

"Esse movimento também era chamado de poesia do mimeógrafo, que é uma maquininha simplesinha. Você põe álcool, roda, imprime, grampeia, faz livrinho e sai vendendo", explica Chico. "O jeito de imprimir já é parte da identidade desse gênero poético. É o único movimento poético, aliás, que tem um sistema de impressão no seu nome."

Parte desses poetas, aliás, migrou para a música e ajudou a formar a cena que explodiria na década seguinte. Bernardo Vilhena, ligado ao coletivo de poesia Nuvem Cigana, escreveu letras para Ritchie e Blitz; Chacal, outro nome da poesia marginal, também fez parcerias com Blitz e Barão Vermelho.

Chico lembra ainda que até movimentos marcados pela ruptura, como o punk, tinham uma dimensão mercadológica. Ele cita os logotipos de bandas como exemplos de uma identidade visual que também servia para criar reconhecimento e circulação. "A questão mercadológica era inescapável", diz.

articles.title: Chuva em Sorocaba: alagamentos, queda de muro e vias interditadas | G1
articles.standfirst: Volume acumulado em 24 horas chegou a 71 milímetros; Rio Sorocaba subiu quase dois metros durante a madrugada.
articles.summary: Chuva em Sorocaba causa alagamentos, interdições em avenidas e queda de muro em canil após o nível do rio subir dois metros durante a madrugada.
articles.body:
Muro do Canil Municipal de Sorocaba — Foto: Divulgação/José Ricardo

A chuva intensa que atingiu Sorocaba (SP) na madrugada deste sábado (12) causou pontos de alagamento em diversos bairros, alagou vias importantes e provocou a queda do muro dos fundos do canil municipal. O acumulado em 24 horas atingiu 71 milímetros, totalizando 214 milímetros no mês de setembro, conforme boletim da Defesa Civil municipal enviado por volta das 8h.

Durante o pico da tempestade, o Rio Sorocaba chegou a ficar quase dois metro acima do nível normal. Ainda pela manhã, o volume de água do rio baixou, registrando 1,10 metro acima do normal na régua da Praça Lions. Não há registro de moradores desabrigados ou desalojados.

A Defesa Civil enviou 15 alertas Cell Broadcast - sistema de mensagem emergencial pelo celular - para as regiões de Itapetininga, Sorocaba, Bauru, São José do Rio Preto e Presidente Prudente.

O muro dos fundos do Canil Municipal desabou por volta das 2h40. A Guarda Civil Municipal (GCM), a Defesa Civil e a equipe responsável pelo manejo dos animais acompanharam a ocorrência. Nenhum animal ficou ferido, e os cães que estavam abrigados no trecho afetado foram remanejados para um local seguro.

Agentes de trânsito e equipes de limpeza da prefeitura trabalham na remoção de lama e galhos. Confira o panorama das vias na cidade:

articles.body:
A varanda de uma casa de Santa Isabel desabou na manhã deste sábado (12), após a cidade registrar chuva durante a madrugada. O caso aconteceu na Rua Paraná, no Parque Santa Teresa. Ninguém ficou ferido.

Imagens de uma câmera de segurança registraram o momento do desabamento. Parte da estrutura caiu em direção ao imóvel vizinho, mas não atingiu a casa (confira acima).

Santa Isabel registrou 67,8 milímetros de chuva durante a madrugada deste sábado (12). Por volta das 9h20, quando a varanda desabou, a chuva já não era tão intensa.

Varanda de casa desaba durante chuva em Santa Isabel — Foto: Reprodução / Defesa Civil

Árvore caiu com a chuva desta madrugada na estrada Monte Negro, em Santa Isabel — Foto: Reprodução / Defesa Civil

A cidade registrou outro desabamento na Rua 7 de Setembro, na região do Jardim Monte Serrat. Segundo a Prefeitura, ninguém ficou ferido.

Uma árvore também caiu durante a madrugada na Estrada Monte Negro.

Arte - Total de chuva previsto para o Alto Tietê — Foto: g1 / Arte

Alagamentos: evite áreas inundadas e não tente atravessar vias com acúmulo de água, mesmo que a profundidade pareça pequena.

Ventos fortes: mantenha distância de árvores, postes, fiação elétrica e estruturas metálicas.

Encostas e morros: fique atento a sinais de deslizamento de terra. Diante de qualquer alteração, procure um local seguro.

Trânsito: reduza a velocidade e aumente a distância de segurança em relação aos demais veículos.

articles.body:
Voo de Brasília para o RJ é cancelado por problemas técnicos — Foto: reprodução

Um voo que partiria de Brasília para o Rio de Janeiro (RJ), na manhã deste sábado (12), foi cancelado por problemas técnicos.

A aeronave deveria partir do Aeroporto de Brasília, às 8h, com destino ao Aeroporto Santos Dumont .

Passageiros relataram ao g1 que entraram na aeronave às 7h, mas ela não chegou a decolar. Eles permaneceram dentro do avião até 9h20, quando foram informados sobre o cancelamento.

Segundo a Gol , a aeronave apresentou problemas técnicos e, por consequência, o voo foi cancelado.

A companhia aérea diz que os clientes "foram reacomodados em novos voos da Companhia durante hoje, operados sem intercorrências".

Uma passageira disse ao g1 o cancelamento gerou uma grande fila no Aeroporto de Brasília. Houve realocações para voos as 15h e 23h.

“Ninguém sabe informar nada pra gente. Estou viajando com meu irmão e minha prima mais novos, e colocaram a gente em voos diferentes. Estou tentando resolver mas não sei mais como fazer”, diz.

articles.title: Motorista presa por matar estudante em Porto Velho ganha liberdade | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão considerou que a investigada tem bons antecedentes, endereço fixo e estuda. Ela usará tornozeleira eletrônica e não poderá dirigir ou beber.
articles.summary: Motorista presa em Porto Velho por matar estudante de jornalismo usará tornozeleira e está proibida de dirigir após decisão da Justiça de Rondônia.
articles.body:
A Justiça de Rondônia concedeu, na sexta-feira (12), um habeas corpus a Stefanny Thalia Ferreira Liberato. Ela foi presa na última semana por atropelar e matar o motociclista João Pedro de Oliveira de Souza , de 21 anos, na Zona Norte de Porto Velho .

Segundo a Justiça, o benefício foi concedido porque a motorista preenche requisitos legais, como não ter antecedentes criminais, possuir endereço e trabalho fixos e frequentar curso superior.

Com a decisão, Stefanny foi liberada sob a condição de ser monitorada por tornozeleira eletrônica. Ela também está proibida de dirigir e de ingerir bebidas alcoólicas.

O atropelamento aconteceu no dia 4 de setembro, no bairro São João Bosco. Câmeras de monitoramento (veja vídeo acima) mostram o momento em que o jipe dirigido por Stefanny avança a preferencial e atinge a motocicleta de João Pedro na via principal. O jovem foi arremessado contra a parede de uma residência, e a mulher fugiu do local.

Policiais relataram que a motorista apresentava sinais de embriaguez, como hálito etílico, olhos avermelhados, sonolência e dificuldade de equilíbrio. De acordo com o boletim de ocorrência, ela assumiu ter bebido antes de dirigir.

O motociclista foi socorrido pelo Corpo de Bombeiros e levado ao Hospital e Pronto-Socorro João Paulo II com sangramento intenso. A equipe médica informou à polícia que o jovem não resistiu aos ferimentos e morreu na unidade.

O g1 tenta localizar a defesa da motorista.

articles.title: In 1900, Chicago engineers reversed the flow of an entire river to push the city's sewage away from Lake Michigan; 126 years later, the river still runs backwards
articles.summary: US News: Chicago's founding problem had always been plumbing. The city drew its drinking water from Lake Michigan and emptied sewers into the Chicago River, wh.
articles.body: Chicago's founding problem had always been plumbing. The city drew its drinking water from Lake Michigan and emptied sewers into the Chicago River, which flowed straight into Lake Michigan. But every rainstorm flushed the stockyards and slaughterhouses and a million people's waste out toward the water intakes. This is why the nineteenth-century city was periodically ravaged by typhoid, cholera, dysentery and more. This is when the city came up with a solution: if the river ends in the wrong place, turn it around.Creating a ditchRivers don't turn around on command. But Chicago is near a low ridge. That ridge separates the Great Lakes basin from the Mississippi River basin. Engineers had a simple idea. Dig a deep ditch towards the Des Plaines River, and gravity would take the water the other way.The tool created to do this was the Chicago Sanitary and Ship Canal, a 28-mile channel cut from the river's South Branch to Lockport, crossing the low subcontinental divide that separates the Great Lakes basin from the Mississippi’s. Dig deep enough, and gravity itself could be re-hired: lake water would pour into the Chicago River, push its whole flow backwards, and carry the city’s diluted sewage away down the Des Plaines and Illinois rivers toward the Mississippi.The digging, from 1892, was the largest earth-moving enterprise the world had then seen, tens of millions of cubic yards of rock and clay, new machines invented for the job, a workforce of thousands. The methods pioneered on what locals called the Big Ditch became known as the Chicago School of Earth Moving, and its veterans and techniques went on to dig the Panama Canal.Calling for troubleDownstream, the plan had been received with understandable horror. Missouri, whose largest city, St. Louis, drank from the Mississippi, saw Chicago preparing to point its sewers at their faucets, and prepared to ask the U.S. Supreme Court for an injunction before the canal could open. Chicago’s sanitary trustees, hearing the lawsuit was coming, chose velocity. On the frigid morning of January 2, 1900, with almost no announcement, they went out to the last earthen dam at Kedzie Avenue and had it cut; one account has trustees attacking the final barrier themselves as the water broke through. By January 17 the controlling works at Lockport were opened and the reversal was fact. Missouri filed within weeks, but there was no longer a construction project to enjoin, only a river already running backwards. A fisherman’s line of that season put it best: the Chicago River had become “the only river in the world that flows away from its mouth.”Missouri pressed the case anyway, and Missouri v. Illinois became a landmark. In 1906, Justice Oliver Wendell Holmes delivered the Court’s answer: Missouri had failed to prove that Chicago’s distant, diluted sewage was what sickened St. Louis, a burden made harder to carry by the awkward fact that St. Louis and every city between were pouring their own raw sewage into the same rivers. The suit failed; the reversal stood. The case, in the process, helped found the federal common law of interstate pollution, the legal machinery later used against actual proven polluters.126 years laterThe reversal delivered exactly what its engineers promised Chicago. With sewage no longer marinating the water intakes, the city’s typhoid and waterborne-disease death rates collapsed within a generation, and the project entered the engineering pantheon, the American Society of Civil Engineers eventually named it a monument of the millennium, alongside the Panama Canal its workers went on to dig.A century and a quarter later, Lake Michigan water flows in at the lakefront and runs backwards through downtown, the reversal maintained by locks and controlling works. In the biggest storms, when even the city’s cavernous Deep Tunnel reservoirs fill, the gates must occasionally be opened, and the river allowed to run the old way into the lake for a few hours. The canal that separated Chicago’s sewage from its drinking water also stitched together two watersheds nature had kept apart, which is why it is now the front line of the Asian carp fight, an electric fish barrier humming in the channel to keep the Mississippi’s invaders out of the Great Lakes.That link works both ways. Fish are now able to swim between what used to be separate basins. According to a University of Illinois study covered by ScienceDaily, invasive Asian carp are moving north through this waterway, heading for Lake Michigan and the rest of the Great Lakes. Researchers pinpointed 18 risky spots along the canal where invasive species could enter. Since then, electric barriers have been installed in the water to help keep the carp out.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Indian-origin woman in Canada arrested after landlord-tenant dispute turned ugly; this is what happened next
articles.summary: Rest of World News: An Indian-origin woman in Canada was arrested after a dispute with her tenant over a barbecue escalated into a series of confrontations at a rental pr.
articles.body: An Indian-origin woman in Canada was arrested after a dispute with her tenant over a barbecue escalated into a series of confrontations at a rental property. The tenant shared videos of the incidents on social media, alleging that his landlady entered his home without permission, removed food from his grill and later interfered with his access to the property. The video had gone viral all over social media.The woman has been identified as Raj Tiwana. The tenant posted the videos on Instagram under the account name Tiwana Farm Survivor. The footage has drawn attention on social media, with several clips showing arguments between the two and a later police arrest. According to a TOI report, the tenant alleged harassment by his landlady in Surrey, Canada.In an update shared by the tenant, police were seen arriving at Tiwana's home. The footage reportedly shows officers telling her that she was under arrest. She appeared confused and asked whether she could call her daughter before being handcuffed and escorted to a police vehicle. The exact charges against Tiwana and the circumstances leading to her arrest were not immediately available in the information provided.Dispute began over cooking food in the gardenAccording to the tenant's account, the confrontation began when he was cooking food on a barbecue in the garden with a friend. Tiwana reportedly objected to the barbecue, saying she could not allow them to cook on her property. In a video shared by the tenant, the woman is seen pointing towards brown marks on a wall. She appeared to be concerned about possible damage to the property.The tenant, who said he was 50 years old, told her that he had the right to have a friend over for dinner because he paid rent. His friend recorded the exchange on a mobile phone. The argument grew heated, with Tiwana also objecting to the presence of the tenant's friend, who was filming the confrontation.The tenant said the marks on the wall were of rust, while the woman reportedly claimed that he was trying to burn her property. She suggested that he could go to his friend's house if he wanted to enjoy a barbecue.Landlady seen removing food from barbecueIn another video from the same day, Tiwana is seen removing food from the grill while the tenant and his friend were preparing dinner. The tenant objected and accused her of trying to intimidate them. According to a TOI report, the woman picked up a piece of wood and pushed the food off the barbecue. She reportedly said she could not allow them to cook on her property and that she would call the police. The incident, which began as an argument over the use of the barbecue, later became part of a wider dispute between the tenant and the landlady.Tenant had shared more videos alleging harassmentAfter the barbecue confrontation, the tenant posted several more videos on Instagram. He alleged that the incident was not isolated and claimed that Tiwana had repeatedly interfered with his use of the rental property. In one video, the woman appears to enter the tenant's home. The footage reportedly shows her throwing rocks in his direction before a physical confrontation. The tenant repeatedly asked her to leave his unit. Another clip appeared to show the woman grabbing a container from a table and striking the tenant's friend while questioning why he was at the property.Tenant alleges forced entry, lock changes and missing doorThe tenant also made allegations about access to his rental unit. He claimed that Tiwana had entered his home in his absence and later changed the locks. In one post, he said his rent had been paid through August 15. He also alleged that the entrance to his rental unit had been left without a door. In a video, the tenant reportedly said the property had been broken into for the third time and that the door had been completely removed.The authenticity of the viral videos had not been independently verified and that police had not issued an official statement on the incident.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: At least 7 Kurds killed in Syria prison riot as tensions flare in Kurdish-held Kobani
articles.summary: Middle East News: At least seven people were killed after a riot and fire broke out at a prison in the predominantly Kurdish town of Kobani in northern Syria on Saturda.
articles.body: At least seven people were killed after a riot and fire broke out at a prison in the predominantly Kurdish town of Kobani in northern Syria on Saturday, highlighting the fragile security situation as Damascus moves to tighten its control over Kurdish-held areas.The fire erupted after inmates at the prison rioted, according to Syria’s state news agency SANA. The incident came amid rising tensions in Kobani between Kurdish and Arab residents. The Britain-based Syrian Observatory for Human Rights said the unrest was linked to plans to transfer some inmates to a prison in Aleppo.The violence follows clashes and protests in Kobani a day earlier after a Kurdish man was allegedly killed by Arabs. The incident triggered anger among Kurdish residents and further heightened tensions in the strategically important border town.The latest unrest also exposes the difficulties involved in the transfer of security responsibilities from Kurdish forces to Syria’s central government. Syrian government troops have entered Kobani, but the prison where the riot occurred remains under the control of Kurdish fighters, underscoring the complicated nature of the transition.Kobani has long held strategic importance in Syria’s war. It became a major battlefield during the fight against Islamic State after the militant group attacked the town in 2014. Kurdish forces, backed by the US-led coalition, eventually drove Islamic State out of Kobani and later played a central role in the campaign that ended the group’s territorial control in Syria.The Kurdish-led, US-backed Syrian Democratic Forces had for years controlled large parts of northeastern Syria and administered a semi-autonomous area. Its commander announced the group’s official dissolution in late August as part of efforts to integrate Kurdish-held territories and security structures with Damascus.However, the developments in Kobani indicate that the process remains fraught with uncertainty. Kurdish forces continue to retain control of some key security facilities even as government forces expand their presence.The prison incident also carries wider security implications because Kurdish authorities have been responsible for guarding thousands of Islamic State-linked detainees. Any disruption during the transition could complicate efforts to secure detention facilities and prevent militant escapes.The violence in Kobani therefore underscores the broader challenge facing Damascus: integrating Kurdish-held areas while preventing renewed ethnic conflict and maintaining security across northern Syria.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Die first, white man': US university probes Nigerian-origin professor Uju Anya's ‘threatening’ social media posts
articles.summary: US News: Carnegie Mellon University has launched a review of social media posts attributed to Nigerian-born professor Uju Anya after a fresh backlash over rema.
articles.body: Carnegie Mellon University has launched a review of social media posts attributed to Nigerian-born professor Uju Anya after a fresh backlash over remarks described by the university as “hostile and threatening”. The university said Anya, an associate professor of second-language acquisition in its Department of Languages, Cultures and Applied Linguistics, is currently on voluntary professional leave and is not teaching on campus during the 2026-27 academic year.“We are deeply concerned by recent hostile and threatening social media posts by Dr. Anya and are reviewing this matter closely,” Carnegie Mellon said in a statement posted on X.The university also clarified that the posts did not represent its views and said they were contrary to its community standards and values, as well as its commitment to maintaining a safe and respectful campus.The controversy centres on a resurfaced exchange on X involving Anya and an account identified as @TheWuhanClan. The exchange starts from a post in February 2021, when Anya commented on the death of conservative US radio host Rush Limbaugh.After the account accused her of celebrating the deaths of white people, Anya responded with a post telling the user to “Die first, white man, then ask yourself why I’m dancing.”The X account later directly addressed the university, alleging that Anya had made similar comments in the past and accusing Carnegie Mellon of failing to discipline her. The account described the latest post as a death threat and demanded that the university “own” the controversy.The issue also drew attention from billionaire Elon Musk, who commented on the controversy on X while identifying Anya as a professor at Carnegie Mellon.Anya’s X account became inaccessible amid the backlash, with reports suggesting that the account had been deactivated. She had not publicly responded to Carnegie Mellon’s latest statements as of Saturday.Meanwhile, Anya made disparaging posts on Charlie Kirk's death anniversary and wished 'Eid al Kirk mubarak'.The latest controversy is not the first time Anya’s social media posts have attracted international attention.In September 2022, she faced widespread criticism after posting comments about the late Queen Elizabeth II shortly before the monarch’s death. Anya accused the British monarchy of representing the legacy of colonialism and blamed Britain for supporting the Nigerian government during the Nigerian Civil War, also known as the Biafran War, from 1967 to 1970.Anya later explained that members of her family had been killed and displaced during the conflict and that the history of British involvement in Nigeria shaped her views of the monarchy. Her comments at the time also drew reactions from Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, who questioned how someone seeking to make the world better could make such remarks.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Brics leaders on Saturday asserted that they recognised women as leaders, decision-makers and key drivers of economic growth and social transformation.In a joint declaration issued after their meeting, the leaders also acknowledged the vital role of women in peacebuilding in line with the global Women, Peace and Security agenda."We affirm that women's participation in governance; their financial and digital inclusion; their capacity building, access to skill development and entrepreneurship opportunities, support to entrepreneurship, access to productive and social services and their crucial role in climate action, food security and nutrition, which are interconnected is key for sustainable development," the declaration said.The leaders also highlighted the importance of policies supporting women's full participation in economic life, including through appropriate care policies in accordance with national circumstances."We also recognise the importance of policies that support women's full participation in economic life, including through appropriate care policies, in accordance with national circumstances," it added.The leaders said they looked forward to the 12th Brics Parliamentary Forum in October 2026, which will include a meeting of women parliamentarians and a meeting of international affairs committee chairpersons."We emphasise the importance of these engagements as useful platforms to enhance mutual understanding and trust among nations, drive innovation and strengthen institutional resilience towards building an inclusive, sustainable and equitable future for all," they said.The declaration also commended the role of the Brics Women's Business Alliance (WBA) in promoting women's entrepreneurship, leadership and economic participation across member countries."We welcome the recommendations in the Annual Report of the Women's Business Alliance that aims at improving access to finance, markets, technology, skills development and digital opportunities for women-led enterprises. We note the strong engagement achieved to date across Brics countries in the WBA's 2026 programmes," the leaders said."We encourage BRICS National Chapters to continue strengthening intra-Brics cooperation on women's economic participation, including through knowledge-sharing and joint initiatives," the declaration added.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: France lifts alcohol content limit on champagne after record heatwaves
articles.summary: Winemakers can produce bubbly up to 15% ABV following an unusual harvest that produced sweeter grapes.
articles.body:
Champagne lovers may find themselves getting tipsy more quickly after French producers have been given the go-ahead to raise the alcohol content in a bottle of bubbly for the first time following this summer's record heatwave.

Winemakers can temporarily produce champagne with an alcohol content of up to 15% - above the 13% cap, industry officials have said.

The extreme heat and drought produced grapes with exceptionally higher sugar levels. Yeast converts sugar into alcohol during fermentation.

France's Champagne region also saw its earliest-ever harvest due to the weather, something that could become the norm "in 10 to 15 years" because of climate change, according to the Comite Champagne industry association.

How will extreme weather affect our food?

France links sharp rise in drownings to heatwaves

The temporary increase in champagne's alcohol content is only expected to affect a small number of wines, a spokeswoman for the Comite Champagne told the BBC.

During the second fermentation process, which gives champagne its bubbles, "a very small number of wines from this harvest could have slightly exceeded the regulatory limit of 13%, reaching around 13.1% or 13.2%".

"Therefore a decision was made to exceptionally and temporarily increase the regulatory limit to 15% - only for this year," she said.

The first grapes were cut in early August and the harvest expanded by the middle of the month, "the earliest ever recorded in Champagne", the association said.

"The 2026 growing season will be remembered as one of the most unusual in Champagne's history, marked by severe spring frosts of historic intensity, an exceptionally early flowering period and five heatwaves throughout the summer." it added.

Speaking in the Times newspaper, Stéphane Vignon, a producer in Verzenay said: "The Mediterranean climate is moving north. This is year one of a new cycle. It's unlikely to be every year, but it will happen again".

Higher-strength champagne is unlikely to be an obvious selling point, warned Jane Anson, a wine columnist and author based in Bordeaux.

She told the Times: "Today people increasingly prefer lower-alcohol

"The battle between what consumers want and what nature provides must be very stressful for producers."

The 2026 vintage is unlikely to hit shelves until 2028 as champagne must age for at least 15 months.

Maxime Toubart, co-chair of the Comite Champagne, told the AFP news agency that the likelihood of hotter weather in the future means "this unusual harvest will probably become the norm in 10 to 15 years".

France has been one of Europe's worst-hit countries during this year's extreme weather, sparking huge wildfires .

Climate change is driving up global average temperatures, making heatwaves more frequent and intense.

It has been felt acutely in Europe, which is the fastest warming continent, heating up twice as fast as the global average, according to the Copernicus climate service.

articles.title: 'Have opportunity to discuss cooperation': PM Modi welcomes Xi; bilateral talks begin
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping held a bilateral meeting lasting more than 50 minutes in New Delhi on Saturda.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping held a bilateral meeting lasting more than 50 minutes in New Delhi on Saturday, shortly after the adoption of the Brics Summit 2026 declaration.The meeting took place on the sidelines of the Brics Summit, where leaders of the grouping adopted the summit declaration following discussions on key global and regional issues.Welcoming Xi, PM Modi thanked China for its support and cooperation during India's Brics chairmanship and said the two sides now had an opportunity to discuss bilateral ties."It gives me great pleasure to extend a warm welcome to you. Thank you very much for your positive remarks at the Brics Summit. I express my gratitude for the support and cooperation received from China during India's Brics chairmanship. We now have the opportunity to discuss bilateral cooperation. Once again, a warm welcome to India."The meeting assumes significance as India and China have sought to stabilise bilateral relations following tensions along their disputed border in recent years. The two leaders have held several engagements aimed at improving ties and maintaining peace and tranquillity along the border.PM Modi welcomes XiDuring the bilateral meeting, PM Modi expressed his gratitude for China's cooperation during India's Brics presidency and welcomed Xi to India."I express my gratitude for the support and cooperation received from China during India's Brics chairmanship. We now have the opportunity to discuss bilateral cooperation. Once again, a warm welcome to India."The meeting followed the conclusion of the Brics summit, which brought together leaders and delegations from member countries, partner nations and outreach invitees in New Delhi.Xi stresses long-term tiesXi told PM Modi that China views India-China relations from a strategic and long-term perspective, according to Xinhua. He said the two countries, as the world's two most populous nations and key members of the Global South, have significant responsibilities amid a complex international landscape.Xi also said India and China should learn from each other's strengths and work towards shared development. During the meeting, he said:"In the face of a complex international landscape marked by intertwined changes and challenges, China and India, as the world's two most populous countries and important members of the Global South, shoulder significant responsibilities. Both sides should keep the future of humanity in mind and the well-being of their peoples at heart, and work together to advance high-quality cooperation within the greater BRICS framework. We should advocate an equal and orderly multipolar world and an inclusive, mutually beneficial form of economic globalisation, injecting more positive energy into the promotion of world peace, stability, development and prosperity."Earlier, the BRICS nations unanimously adopted the New Delhi Declaration 2026, which expressed deep concern over the continued escalation of tensions in West Asia and called for maximum restraint and avoidance of actions that could further aggravate the situation.“We urge to ensure the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure in accordance with the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations in their entirety and interconnectedness, including respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the States,” the declaration said.The BRICS declaration also encouraged greater efforts through dialogue and diplomacy towards a long-term understanding contributing to lasting peace, security and stability in the region.“We stress the need to work together to maintain smooth flow of global trade, supply chains and energy, in accordance with applicable international law,” it said.The grouping expressed serious concern over deliberate attacks on civilian infrastructure and peaceful nuclear facilities under full safeguards of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), stressing that nuclear safeguards, safety and security must be upheld, including during armed conflicts.The declaration also called for implementation of relevant UN General Assembly and UN Security Council resolutions and urged all parties to ensure the maintenance of ceasefire and full and unhindered humanitarian access in the Gaza Strip.Addressing the BRICS Summit, Xi Jinping called on BRICS nations to play a peacemaking role amid the conflict in West Asia, saying China would work with other members towards that goal.The BRICS declaration also noted the current global context of polarisation and distrust and encouraged global action to strengthen international peace and security. It advocated a multilateral approach that respects diverse national viewpoints on key global issues, including sustainable development, eradication of hunger and poverty and the global response to climate change.The grouping also expressed concern over growing nuclear risks and conflict and reiterated the need to strengthen the system of disarmament, arms control and non-proliferation to promote global stability and international peace and security.Earlier, addressing the 18th BRICS Summit session on Inclusive Global Governance and Strengthening in New Delhi, PM Modi proposed 10 measures for global governance reform, which BRICS members could develop into a BRICS Reform Roadmap by the next Summit.He also called for transforming the Global South from a “rule-taker into a rule-shaper”, saying the Global South remains at the forefront of global crises but continues to remain on the sidelines when it comes to decision-making.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Divine triumph’: Iran celebrates Houthis’ capture of Yemen’s Red Sea coast
articles.summary: Iranian officials have praised the Houthis’ victories but have not spoken about any imminent closure of Bab al-Mandeb.
articles.body:
Tehran, Iran – Iranian authorities and state media have praised the Houthis’ capture of Yemen’s Red Sea coast, which some see as giving Tehran more leverage against the United States.

The Houthis, a political and armed group dominated by Zaidi Shia Muslims, have been fighting against the Western-backed Yemeni government since capturing the capital, Sanaa, in 2014.

The Houthis captured a series of Red Sea coastal cities and islands this week, essentially giving them control over the vital Bab al-Mandeb strait.

The Iran-allied group’s recent victories have been praised in Iran, and are viewed by some as part of Tehran’s wider war against the US, ongoing since February 28.

“The victories of Yemen’s Ansar Allah in the western coast is a narrative of a divine triumph and the fruit of years of steadfastness in the most difficult of battlefields,” Hossein Mohebbi, spokesman of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), wrote on X on Saturday.

Amid the Houthis’ recent battlefield wins against the fragmented Saudi-backed forces, senior Iranian officials have cheered their Yemeni allies on.

The Houthis’ capture of the port city of Mocha on Friday delivered a huge blow for the Yemeni government, which now has no direct access to the Red Sea.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iranian parliament speaker and chief negotiator with Washington, reposted a comment made by slain Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in 2024, saying the “resistance” of the Houthis will inevitably lead to victory.

“The brave Yemeni people will certainly triumph, by permission of God Almighty,” Ghalibaf added on Thursday, in Arabic.

Iran’s First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref said the government is happy with the Houthi advances, and urged leaders in the region to pursue “the rationality of liberation from dependency [from the US and the West], and unity under the banner of Islam”.

The “grand victory” of the Houthis once again proved that “security is not a commodity that can be bought,” added Mohammad Mokhber, an adviser to Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei.

The Houthis began to attack several vessels in the Red Sea they claimed were linked to Israel in 2023, as part of their stated aim to pressure Israel to end the genocidal war on Gaza.

This prompted bombing campaigns by the US, United Kingdom and Israel against Houthi positions in Sanaa, Hodeidah and other areas.

Saudi Arabia, which joined the war against the Houthis in 2015, has largely stayed out of the current eruption in fighting in Yemen.

After their recent victories, the Yemeni group can now exercise more control over the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandeb strait.

The Houthis’ control of Yemen’s Red Sea coastline and multiple islands – including the island of Mayun, also known as Perim, sitting about 3km (1.9 miles) off Yemen’s mainland – provides the group with close-range access to the Bab al-Mandeb strait.

A video published on Friday showed a Houthi commander telling soldiers they will no longer need missiles and drones to threaten shipping in the crucial waterway. They could simply position artillery along the coast and fire in all directions at ships, he said.

The Houthis have not declared the strait closed, but the group’s military spokesperson, Yahya Saree, said on Friday that “maritime navigation is safe for all companies except for Saudi vessels.”

Likewise, Iran’s partial control of the Strait of Hormuz on the other side of the Arabian Peninsula has been a key tool of leverage for Tehran in the war against the US.

The prospect of closing down the strait could potentially be used by Tehran in future negotiations over ending the war with the US.

Iranian officials are expected to meet regional Arab representatives on Monday for talks over how to facilitate shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, which Tehran maintains remains closed.

They have said they favour a collective regional approach on passage through the strategic waterway.

Iran claims it has reached an understanding with Oman , which also has territorial waters in the strait.

The US, which has continued its naval blockade of Iran’s ports and intensified sanctions on Tehran, reportedly opposes the agreement.

Authorities in Tehran have signalled there will be no talks with Washington under the current circumstances.

“As long as the American side does not accept all of Iran’s conditions, dialogue and negotiation are of no use,” Ebrahim Azizi, head of the hardline Iranian parliament’s national security commission, wrote on X on Saturday.

At the start of the working week in Iran on Saturday, hardline and IRGC-linked newspapers and media outlets celebrated the recent Houthi advances.

Keyhan, whose editor-in-chief was appointed by Ali Khamenei, called the advances “the miracle of resistance” and said they had “put the US and Israel in a bind”.

The Quds newspaper, published by the influential Astan-e Quds Razavi in Mashhad , called Iran and the Houthis “the lord of the straits”.

But even though Tehran has repeatedly threatened that Bab al-Mandeb could be further disrupted if the war continues, Iran’s diplomatic apparatus did not immediately link the Houthi advances with the current fight against the US.

As has often been the case, Iran’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs insisted that the Houthis make their decisions independent of Tehran, with their own interests at heart, including ending Saudi Arabia’s blockade on Yemen.

The Iranian Foreign Ministry also called for an end to the Saudi siege on Houthi-controlled areas, an immediate return to negotiations between the group and Riyadh, and respect for Yemen’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.

The ministry also pushed back on the idea that the Houthis act merely as a proxy for Tehran.

“What is happening now in Yemen is the result of the Yemenis losing patience,” Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei told state television on Friday night.

“It is not fair to ignore the fact that they were under a cruel blockade for years, and concluded that the United Nations and regional mechanisms could not resolve the issues.”

articles.title: Train derails in France and injures 44 as authorities investigate possible sabotage
articles.summary: French authorities are investigating whether sabotage caused a train derailment that injured 44 people in Normandy, after a piece of rail was found on the track, police told The Associated Press on Saturday.
articles.body: French authorities are investigating whether sabotage caused a train derailment that injured 44 people in Normandy, after a piece of rail was found on the track, police told The Associated Press on Saturday. The regional train was carrying 186 passengers from Rouen to Caen when it derailed Friday evening at Cléon, in the Seine-Maritime department of northwestern France. An 18-year-old woman was among the injured and was evacuated by helicopter to Rouen University Hospital, police said. A spokeswoman for the French national police communications service, known as SICOP, said that the piece of rail found on the track was “probably” linked to the derailment. Investigators were working to establish whether the circumstances were accidental or involved sabotage, the service said. The prosecutor’s office remained cautious about drawing conclusions, according to the police. France’s previous rail disasters include the July 2013 derailment at Brétigny-sur-Orge, south of Paris, which killed seven people. In November 2015, a high-speed TGV train carrying out tests derailed at Eckwersheim, near Strasbourg, killing 11. More recently, a crash involving two high-speed trains at Adamuz in southern Spain killed 46 people and injured more than 100 in January, according to the Andalusian regional government.

The IDF responded to a confrontation between several Palestinians and Israeli settlers near Ma'aleh Gilboa in northern Israel after a group of Palestinians reportedly threw stones at a shepherd on Saturday.

Upon arriving at the scene of the incident, IDF soldiers attempted to detain the individuals suspected of throwing the stones and fired shots into the air.

articles.title: In 1984, Steve Jobs bought a 30-room, 17,250-sq-ft California mansion; after years of legal battles, it was demolished in 2011, while its pipe organ and historic fixtures were salvaged
articles.summary: News News: For a house that once embodied California wealth and architectural ambition, the end came not with a grand renovation but with bulldozers. The Jacklin.
articles.body: For a house that once embodied California wealth and architectural ambition, the end came not with a grand renovation but with bulldozers. The Jackling House, a sprawling Spanish Colonial Revival mansion in the wealthy Silicon Valley town of Woodside, became the center of a years-long fight between Steve Jobs and preservationists. According to an online report by Fortune and Architectural Record, Jobs wanted it gone and hoped to replace it with a smaller, more modern home. Preservationists saw something very different: a rare piece of California architectural history worth saving. In the end, Jobs got his way. The 17,250-square-foot mansion was demolished in 2011, although many of its historic fixtures were salvaged before the building disappeared.A grand home with an unusual pastThe house was commissioned in the 1920s by Daniel C. Jackling, a self-made copper millionaire whose business transformed the American copper industry. Architect George Washington Smith designed the residence, drawing on Spanish and Andalusian influences to create a massive white-stucco estate with the character of an old European village, states the online report.Built in 1926, the mansion featured 30 rooms, including 14 bedrooms, and occupied six acres. Its construction incorporated a distinctive double-wall system designed to provide insulation while giving the structure the heavy appearance of traditional adobe buildings.Inside, the house was equally elaborate. Thousands of handmade Tunisian and Spanish tiles covered parts of the interior, while dark timber beams, wide-plank white oak floors, custom copper hardware and ornate chandeliers added to its old-world character and according to a report by the Fortune, an aeolian pipe organ was among its most unusual features.Jobs takes on the mansionAccording to Architectural Record, Jobs purchased the property in 1984, when he was 29 and Apple was preparing to launch the Macintosh. He reportedly paid about $2 million for the estate and lived there for roughly a decade before eventually moving to Palo Alto. Despite its architectural pedigree, Jobs disliked the sprawling mansion and considered it impractical for his lifestyle. He eventually envisioned replacing it with a much smaller residence designed around his own preferences and the needs of his family.A battle over preservationBecause the mansion was more than 50 years old, its proposed demolition came under review through California's environmental and historic preservation laws. A subsequent assessment determined that the property was eligible for the California Register of Historical Resources. Preservationists organized against the demolition, arguing that Smith's work represented an important chapter in American architecture. The dispute moved through the courts, reaching the California Supreme Court after an earlier demolition attempt was challenged, adds the online report.Jobs also offered an alternative, where anyone willing to relocate the enormous house could potentially take it. Several preservation-minded parties explored the possibility, but the relocation plans never came together. As the legal battle continued, the empty property deteriorated. The house sat largely unused, exposed to the elements and increasingly difficult to restore.The mansion comes downBy 2008, Jobs had revised his plans and again sought permission to demolish the structure. The proposal compared the cost and difficulty of restoring the deteriorated mansion with building a significantly smaller replacement home and this time, the legal challenge failed. The demolition permit was eventually issued, and in 2011 the Jackling House was reduced to rubble, ending one of Silicon Valley's most unusual preservation disputes.Yet the story did not end entirely with the wrecking equipment. Many of the home's historic fittings were removed and preserved, including Victorian-era marble sinks, handmade tiles and other architectural elements. The famous pipe organ was also salvaged. The mansion itself was gone, but pieces of its history survived, scattered remnants of a grand California estate that had spent years caught between preservation and the desire to build something new.Images Courtesy: Facebook, Architectural Records, and SFGATEReady to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: In 1930 she took her first college course during the Great Depression, in 2007, she finally received her Bachelor's degree: How Nola Ochs became one of 'world's oldest graduate'?
articles.summary: US News: When 21-year-old Alexandra walked across the stage at Fort Hays State University in 2007 to collect her bachelor's degree, she had a rather unusual fe.
articles.body: When 21-year-old Alexandra walked across the stage at Fort Hays State University in 2007 to collect her bachelor's degree, she had a rather unusual fellow graduate beside her. Her grandmother, Nola Ochs, was also receiving a degree that day. The difference was that Alexandra was 21 and Ochs was 95.For Ochs, the ceremony marked the end of a journey that had begun 77 years earlier, when she took her first college course at the same Kansas institution in 1930. She had started her education during the Great Depression, then spent decades teaching, farming, raising a family and eventually returning to the classroom. By the time she finally received her bachelor's degree, she had lived through some of the biggest events of the 20th century.But the extraordinary part of her story was not simply that she went back to college at 95. It was that she treated her age as little more than a number. Ochs first enrolled at what is now Fort Hays State University on April 19, 1930, when it was still a Kansas teachers' college. She went on to teach in rural Kansas schools before marrying Vernon Ochs and raising four sons. College was put on hold as family and farm life took priority.Decades passed. After her husband died, however, Ochs returned to her studies. She began taking classes part-time at Dodge City Community College while continuing to work toward the degree she had left unfinished many years earlier. Eventually, she discovered that she was only 30 credit hours short of a bachelor's degree. The finish line was finally within sight.But rather than simply completing the remaining credits from home, Ochs decided to return to Fort Hays State University itself. At 95, she moved from her farm into a campus apartment and became a student again.She took classes alongside students young enough to be her grandchildren, completing the coursework required for her degree. Her age attracted attention, but Ochs herself seemed far less interested in the novelty of being a nonagenarian college student.Speaking to CBS News, she recalled that she knew she was old when she arrived on campus, but chose not to dwell on it. “When I came up here of course I knew I was old, but I didn’t pay attention to how old I was,” she said. And when asked about her experience as a student, she offered an even simpler explanation: “I was just another student.”Her granddaughter Alexandra was studying at Fort Hays State at the same time. In 2007, the two women graduated together, turning what might already have been an extraordinary academic milestone into a family moment. “I’m really happy to be able to do this with her,” Alexandra said.For Ochs, the bachelor's degree was the completion of something she had started nearly eight decades earlier. At 95, Ochs became the world’s oldest college graduate. That is the part that made the news. But she was not finished learning.Three years after earning her bachelor's degree, Ochs returned to the classroom once again. At 98, she earned a master's degree in liberal studies from Fort Hays State University.She continued taking classes until she turned 100, eventually returning to her farm. By then, her academic journey had stretched across seven decades.Ochs had begun college in 1930, when the country was entering the depths of the Great Depression. She returned to higher education after raising four sons, losing her husband and spending years away from formal studies.Her story was not simply about finishing an unfinished degree.The bachelor's degree could have been viewed as closing a chapter that had remained open since 1930. But pursuing a master's degree at 98 made it clear that Ochs was not merely trying to complete something she had left behind. She genuinely wanted to keep learning.Her decision to move into student housing at 95 is perhaps the most striking part of the story. She did not ask the university to make an exception for her or simply accept an honorary qualification. She enrolled, lived on campus and completed the same kind of coursework as the other students.The years between her first college class and her graduation were filled with the ordinary responsibilities of life. She taught children, married, raised a family, worked on a farm and dealt with loss.Her education simply waited. When she finally returned to it, she found that the classroom was still there.Ochs died in 2016 at the age of 105. Her name remains tied to one of the most unusual graduation stories in American higher education: a woman who entered college during the Great Depression, took a 77-year detour through life and returned to finish what she had started.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Pentagon seeks AI system to detect, assess missile threats in 2 seconds before the clock runs out
articles.summary: International News: The Pentagon is seeking an artificial intelligence system capable of identifying and assessing space and missile threats within seconds, aiming to tur.
articles.body: The Pentagon is seeking an artificial intelligence system capable of identifying and assessing space and missile threats within seconds, aiming to turn fragmented sensor data into actionable military intelligence before critical response time runs out.The US defence Innovation Unit (DIU) has invited proposals for a “Space Threat Intelligence Synthesis Engine” that would combine live video, satellite imagery, radar and sensor feeds, geospatial data and classified intelligence reports into a continuously updated threat picture.The proposed system is expected to process incoming information and produce “actionable, confidence-scored alerts” that can support human analysts, human-supervised operations or automated workflows.According to the DIU solicitation, existing systems “struggle to distinguish closely spaced objects, track emerging threats, and keep threat models current.” The Pentagon wants AI software that can overcome these limitations and provide a “continuously updated understanding of space and missile threats fast enough to drive operational decisions.”DIU wants the system to process data and display results with a latency of no more than five seconds, with two seconds as the preferred objective. It should handle regular data streams of around 20 to 30 megabytes per minute and bursts of up to 5 gigabytes per minute.Why every second mattersMissile defence involves several stages, including detection, identification, tracking, threat assessment, decision-making and interceptor launch. Information from multiple sensors must be processed and correlated before an incoming threat can be assessed and a response initiated.The Pentagon's push for faster AI processing reflects the growing volume and complexity of data generated by missile and drone attacks. Human operators can face significant challenges when they have to rapidly analyse information from radar, satellites, video and other intelligence sources.AI could shorten this decision cycle by processing multiple feeds simultaneously, correlating information and updating threat assessments in real time. Instead of waiting for analysts to manually piece together a threat picture, the system could generate confidence-scored alerts and highlight emerging threats within seconds.The Pentagon's preferred two-second processing target could potentially provide commanders and defensive systems with additional time to assess an incoming threat and respond.Human oversight remains centralThe proposed system is not designed to eliminate human involvement. DIU says the technology should support “analyst-in-the-loop, human-on-the-loop, or automated workflows”, allowing the level of human involvement to vary according to operational requirements.The system would provide operators with human-readable threat visualisations and confidence-scored alerts, while AI would handle the rapid processing and correlation of large volumes of data.The broader objective is to reduce the time analysts spend assembling and interpreting fragmented information, while retaining human oversight over monitoring and decision-making in critical military operations.
